The main tradeoffs identified were response time versus schedulability, simplicity versus implementation complexity, runtime overhead versus better responsiveness, and formal guarantees versus practical deployability.

The uploaded lecture shows that scheduling is part of architecture exploration and design decisions in embedded systems. entries.objective: To understand the main engineering tradeoffs between Sporadic Server and related scheduling methods.
entries.prompt: okay now I want to to write the tradeoff analysis part of Milestone 2 for Sporadic Server, help me how i could go through the tradeoffs in a simple way? I want to compare response time, schedulability runtime overhead memory overhead etc. and practical use in embedded systems just give me the points so that I can check and rewrite.
entries.ai_output_summary: The LLM explained that the main tradeoff is between fast aperiodic response and protection of periodic hard real-time tasks. Background scheduling is simple and safe for periodic tasks but gives poor aperiodic response. Polling Server is simple but may waste capacity. Deferrable Server improves response time but can increase interference. Sporadic Server gives controlled responsiveness but needs more bookkeeping for budget and replenishment. The AI also mentioned runtime overhead, memory for queues, timer management, and implementation complexity.

actions: I checked whether the tradeoffs match the Milestone 2 task description. The milestone asks for tradeoffs such as runtime, memory, feasibility, and guarantees. I also compared the ideas with real-time scheduling lecture material and my Milestone 1 understanding.

issues: The tradeoff explanation is still general. The exact schedulability claims and replenishment behavior of Sporadic Server must be verified from academic sources before final submission.

entries.reflection: This interaction helped me understand that Milestone 2 should not only list related methods. It should explain what is gained and what is lost when choosing one method over another. I will use these points to write my own tradeoff analysis.
